rows.answer: Yes, you can reach the Wonderland platform step-free from Revere Beach. The current route involves taking the Blue Line to Beachmont, changing platforms, and returning to Wonderland. Please note that this route relies on several lifts, including 884, 886, and 887, which are currently operational. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

Three platforms lose step-free access in the open-data model due to current elevator closures. These include platforms at Downtown Crossing (affected by the closure of elevator 869) and Kendall/MIT (affected by the closure of elevator 777). Additionally, State station has a platform affected by the closure of elevator 803. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

The closure of elevator 711 at Wonderland station does not cut off any stations or journeys from the step-free network in the open-data model. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

Due to today's closures, lifts 813 at Alewife, 884 at Revere Beach, and 922 at Chinatown have become the last step-free link for 176 journeys each. If any of these three lifts were to close, their respective stations would lose step-free access in the open-data model. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

South Station platforms generally have multiple step-free routes available. For the Red Line platforms (Ashmont/Braintree and Airport), there are 2 certified lift routes each. The Bus Terminal gates typically have 3 certified lift routes. Commuter Rail tracks at South Station are at-grade and do not rely on lifts for access. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

At North Station, the Oak Grove platform relies on lift 911 as its only step-free access point. Additionally, the Copley & West platform and the Forest Hills platform both depend on lift 910. If these lifts are out of service, the respective platforms lose step-free access in the open-data model. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

If lift 813 fails, the Red Line platforms at Alewife lose step-free access in the open-data model. No step-free route exists in the open-data model for these platforms while this lift is closed. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

If lift 922 closes, the Chinatown Forest Hills platform loses step-free access in the open-data model. No step-free route exists in the open-data model for this platform under these conditions. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

A step-free route from Airport to Revere Beach is available by taking the Blue Line to Wonderland, turning around, and returning to Revere Beach. This route relies on lift 884 at Revere Beach to reach the street. Please note that several other lifts across the system are currently closed, which may affect your travel. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

Your step-free journey from South Station to Alewife depends on lifts 926, 918, and 919 at South Station, and lifts 813 and 814 at Alewife. There is currently no alternative step-free route that avoids these specific lifts. Please ensure these lifts are operational before you travel. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

The Wonderland-bound platform at Revere Beach loses step-free access in the open-data model due to the closure of lift 885. To exit step-free, you can ride the Blue Line to Wonderland, change platforms, and return to the Revere Beach Bowdoin-bound platform. From there, you can use lift 884 to reach the street level. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.
Yes, there is a step-free route from North Station to Back Bay using the Orange Line. The journey takes approximately 19 minutes and utilizes lifts 912, 910, and 853. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.

Chinatown Elevator 876 should be prioritized for repair as it is currently closed and causes platforms to lose step-free access in the open-data model. Revere Beach Elevator 885 and Back Bay Elevator 854 are also closed and should be addressed immediately. These lifts are ranked highest because their closures directly impact station accessibility. Check mbta.com/alerts/access.
